yt.title: A 3x3 puzzle cube has {c_q} quintillion positions #Shorts
yt.description:
Positions reachable by turning a standard 3x3x3 puzzle cube: 8! x 3^7 x 12! x 2^11 / 2 = {c_n}, computed in Python. Any position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer (half-turn metric), proven in 2010 by Rokicki, Kociemba, Davidson and Dethridge.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: This little puzzle cube fits in your hand. Guess how many ways it can be scrambled.

scenes.label: positions of a 3 by 3 puzzle cube
scenes.narration: More than {c_q_say} quintillion. That is a forty three followed by eighteen more digits.
Eight corners can be arranged and twisted. Twelve edges can be arranged and flipped. Multiply it all, then remove the states no turn can reach.

scenes.text: Yet 20 moves solve any of them
scenes.narration: Yet every single one can be solved in twenty moves or fewer. That was proven in twenty ten, with a lot of computer time.
